transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Noah Park (Redwood CSM), Raj Patel (SummitPay Head of ML), Sara Gomez (Platform Eng), Tom Lee (CTO), Aisha Khan (Security)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Redwood ran through Optimize features focusing on batching and prefix / K V cache recommendations to reduce per-token cost while meeting SummitPay latency SLOs. Discussed sample cost model numbers for hosted vs dedicated, trade-offs (latency vs throughput), KV cache hit-rate assumptions, quantization impact, and next steps to run benchmarks and share a spreadsheet.

Topics: batching strategies, KV cache (prefix cache) sizing, cost model assumptions, dedicated vs hosted, pilot benchmarks, security/compliance checklist

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, um I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. Liam is our solutions engineer, he'll take the deep dive on Optimize and cost model.
[00:12] Raj: Morning, thanks Maya, appreciate it — out of curiosity we'll probably — yeah this is Raj, I'm head of ML at SummitPay. We're mostly focused on payments flows, average convo length is short but we have spikes during support windows.
[00:22] Liam: great thanks Raj, quick agenda: we'll do a quick recap of current Redwood Optimize recommendations, then key batching and prefix/KV cache settings, show the cost model with a couple of example configs, and close with next steps.
[00:34] Sara: quick Q up front — latency target is 150ms p95 for interactive flows, some async jobs can be higher. Wanted to confirm that is feasible with caching.
[00:44] Liam: short answer yes, with a high KV cache hit rate for prefix-heavy requests. We'll show numbers.
[00:48] Tom: one ask, we need to see hosted vs dedicated TCO; also can we quantify the tradeoff where we increase batching to save cost but risk missing SLAs?
[00:58] Liam: totally, that's the core of the cost model. We'll be explicit about batch sizes, effective tokens/s, and the latency SLO headroom.

[05:12] Liam: alright slide one, so Optimize recommends two levers: automatic batching (continuous batching) and prefix/KV caching. For SummitPay where prompts share common prefixes (greeting, transaction metadata) you can get large hit rates if you cache prefixes. Note: transcript sometimes says K V cash — that's just the auto-transcript.
[05:32] Raj: yeah majority of our flows start with the same 60-80 tokens of context, then user message is short. So sounds promising.

[07:20] Liam: example config A (hosted, low-latency focus): model x-large (quantized), batch size target 8, no aggressive batching, KV cache enabled with projected hit-rate 45%. Latency p95 ~ 140-170ms depending on hw region, cost per 1M tokens approx $95 (model + infra) — this is approximate, depends on real hit-rate.
[07:48] Sara: can you explain how the KV cache hit-rate maps to cost reduction?
[07:55] Liam: sure — if you cache prefixes, each cached token doesn't consume model compute. So 45% hit-rate means 45% fewer tokens processed end-to-end; but there's also overhead for cache lookup and network (small). So cost per effective token drops roughly proportional to (1 - hit_rate). On top of that, batching multiplies throughput; with higher batching we amortize kernel launch overhead.

[09:34] Maya: just to add, Optimize gives recommendations automatically by analyzing trace, we simulate hit-rate ranges (eg 20/45/70%) and show cost curves. We'll attach the spreadsheet.

[11:02] Liam: example config B (dedicated, cost-optimized): model x-large quant-4, larger batch target 32 with continuous batching, KV cache hit-rate assumed 60% for prefix-heavy traffic, expected throughput 5k tokens/s per GPU and effective per-1M-token cost ~ $45 with p95 latency in the 180-250ms band — note if you need 150ms p95 you'll want to tune batching window smaller or use more GPUs to keep headroom.

[12:10] Raj: that delta is big — $95 vs $45 per 1M tokens — is that mostly quantization + batching?
[12:18] Liam: yeah it's combination: quantization reduces model compute, dedicated hardware and continuous batching increase utilization; cache hit-rate compounds the savings. Also reserved capacity pricing for Dedicated lowers unit infra cost.

[14:00] Speaker 1: (inaudible) the other thing is KV cache size — how big do we need to provision?
[14:07] Liam: good question. For prefix caching we typically store the KV entries for the prefix length you want to reuse. For SummitPay, prefixes ~80 tokens. If you have 100k active prefixes you'd need to size storage accordingly; typical memory per token per model is N bytes, but Optimize will estimate exact memory and recommend per-pool configs. We'll include an estimate in the sheet.

[16:45] Sara: what's the invalidation policy for cache when user-specific metadata changes? we don't want cross-user leakage.
[16:52] Noah: yes security note — Redwood supports namespacing of cache keys by customer and route, and optional per-conversation KV scoping so you only share safe prefixes. We'll demo the console settings later.

[19:20] Liam: walking through the cost model spreadsheet now — assumptions column: request distribution (70% short interactive, 30% long), avg tokens/user ~120, prefix length 60, hit-rate scenarios 20/45/70. Then compute rows: tokens_sent, tokens_skipped, GPU compute seconds, cost per GPU-hour, amortized tokens per GPU-hour, etc.
[20:02] Raj: can you show sensitivity if hit-rate drops to 25%?
[20:08] Liam: yes, on the sheet that moves config B from $45 to about $80 per 1M tokens. So the point is caching assumptions matter a lot.

[22:30] Tom: on the dedicated side, how do autoscaling and burst capacity work? during billing spikes do we pay more?
[22:39] Liam: Dedicated has reserved baseline plus burst pool. Billing: committed capacity is a flat monthly, burst is usage-based. We'll model both in TCO. For short spikes we try to use pre-warmed capacity to avoid cold starts. There is also the option of per-route fallback to hosted for overflow.

[25:10] Sara: about quantization — does that impact quality? our transaction routing model needs to not hallucinate amounts etc.
[25:18] Liam: quantization (eg 4-bit or mixed) can have minor delta in output quality depending on model & prompt. Optimize has a qual-monitoring workflow: we run evals on a prompt suite (we recommend 500-1k representative examples) to compute regression metrics; if quality drops beyond threshold we fallback to a higher-precision variant. We'll include the eval plan in the next email.

[28:00] Liam: important note on batching vs latency: continuous batching collects requests for a short window (ms) to form larger micro-batches. If you increase collection window to 20-30ms you can get larger batches but add that much queuing latency. For SummitPay 150ms p95 we generally target <8-12ms batching window plus model inference time.

[31:55] Raj: any concrete guidance on batch size? our traffic spikes to 500-800 rps occasionally.
[32:03] Liam: for that RPS you might see effective batch sizes of 16-64 depending on concurrency and model token-length. On Dedicated you can set a max_batch_size and a max_delay_ms. Optimize will recommend those values given trace. For example we recommend max_batch_size 32, max_delay_ms 12 for mixed traffic; but again depends.

[34:40] Maya: question from Aisha earlier — can you repeat data residency / logging behavior when KV cache is enabled?
[34:47] Liam: yes. Cache data follows the same tenancy rules: customer-owned cache buckets, optional encryption at rest with KMS, logs are auditable and can be forwarded to your SIEM. For Private deployments we can keep cache entirely on-prem. We'll share the security doc.

[36:30] Aisha: do you retain user inputs in the cache? how long?
[36:35] Noah: retention is configurable; default TTL for cached prefixes is short (minutes-hours) but you can set per-route TTL and explicit invalidation. We also recommend hashing of sensitive tokens and namespacing to avoid PII exposure.

[39:10] Liam: showing a simulated benchmark: hosted small-batch config - p50/p95 latency 60ms/160ms, throughput ~2k tokens/s, cost ~ $0.10 per 1k tokens equivalent (numbers simplified). Dedicated large-batch config - p50/p95 90ms/210ms with higher throughput 5k tokens/s, cost ~ $0.045 per 1k tokens. Again these are sample numbers and depend on hit-rate.

[41:00] Raj: how do you validate hit-rate assumptions before committing?
[41:05] Liam: best practice: run a dry-run with Optimize - we take a trace and simulate caching on it and show expected hit-rate. Then we run a short benchmark (1-2 hours) to validate in real infra. That's why we asked for 3 representative traces.

[42:40] Tom: what about fallback policies if cache miss spikes cause latency blips?
[42:46] Liam: Redwood supports circuit-breaker style fallbacks and per-route multi-variant policy: if latency or error spikes exceed thresholds we can route to a lower-latency variant or to hosted fallbacks. These are configurable in the Console rollouts tab.

[45:55] Sara: any gotchas with prefix caching and multi-tenant keys? we have per-user context plus account-level context.
[46:02] Liam: yep — do not cache user-specific PII; cache only safe prefixes (system prompts, templates). For account-level context you can namespace by account ID. We'll note this in the security checklist.

[48:10] Maya: ok quick recap and concrete next steps — we'll send the cost model spreadsheet and the Optimize recommendations based on your traces; Liam will run the benchmark for the two configs; Aisha we'll share SOC2 and KMS docs. SummitPay to confirm traces and SLOs.

[49:00] Raj: sounds good, timeline looks reasonable. We'll aim to get traces by Monday.

[50:12] Liam: one tiny note on telemetry: to measure real-world hit-rate we recommend instrumenting the SDK to emit cache-hit metrics and sample prompts. Optimize console can ingest those metrics to refine recommendations.

[51:20] Tom: can you include an example of how to name the cache keys and a small diagram?
[51:28] Liam: yes on the doc we'll include key-naming best-practices: route|account|prefix-hash|version.

[52:05] Maya: alright thanks everyone, we'll send follow-ups. Any final Qs?
[52:12] Aisha: just one — is there an NDA scoping doc for pilot?
[52:17] Maya: we have a standard pilot addendum, I'll attach.

[53:00] Tom: thanks all, appreciate it.
[53:05] Maya: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes/References: will attach slide deck link (doc: redwood.com/decks/optimize-summitpay), cost spreadsheet link (sheet: drive.redwood/optimize-summitpay-cost-model), security docs link (redwood.com/security/summitpay-pack).
